open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: Until the second release the owner meets the review's purpose by hand, from the governance's schedule.
open_points.question: What exact first-release actions let the owner find every customer and archived project due for review, what information do they show, and how does the owner know the review is complete or has failed?
options: The owner interface enumerates all review candidates with the relationship-end or archive date, and the owner compares them with the schedule.
The owner inspects every customer and project individually and calculates what is due.
The owner maintains an external list and uses Registry only for the resulting erase, anonymise or restriction actions.
open_points.default_guess: Expose the relevant dates and marks through existing owner reads and require the owner to inspect and compare all records manually.

witness.initial: The first release contains an archived project whose retention period has elapsed.
events: The owner begins the periodic review using the governance schedule.
The owner uses the first-release owner interface to look for records requiring action.
outcomes: The interface exposes an enumerable set with archive dates, so the owner finds the project.
The interface exposes dates only after individual records are already known, so the owner misses the project unless an external list identifies it.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.question: Does the first-release workaround and accepted visibility gap end when the second release's specification change starts, when that release is admitted, or when it is deployed to production?
options: When the second-release change starts, immediately after the first release is admitted.
When the second release is admitted by the Code Factory.
When the second release is deployed and its counters and review page are operating in production.
open_points.default_guess: The workaround and gap continue until the second release is deployed and operating in production.

witness.initial: The first release has just been admitted, so the second-release change has started, but no second-release code has been designed or deployed.
events: The owner performs the next retention review.
outcomes: Because the second release has started, the stated interim arrangements have ended even though neither counters nor a review page exists.
The interim arrangements continue until the second-release features are deployed.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: The signs of an attempt that only Registry tells apart — a sign-in lockout, a call with a token Registry does not know, a token asking beyond its rights, Kernel's calls outside a session's set — stay unseen by the owner until then
open_points.question: Is this list exhaustive, or does the owner's accepted first-release gap also cover ordinary refused sign-ins, calls naming an unregistered session, and project operations with neither a named nor an active project?
options: The list is exhaustive; omitted refusal kinds need some other owner-visible handling in the first release.
The list is illustrative; every refusal distinguishable only by Registry remains unseen.
Only the refusal kinds counted by R0-97 are covered, and each omitted case must be classified explicitly.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as illustrative and leave every Registry-only refusal unseen until the counters are deployed.

witness.initial: The first release is running and no sign-in lockout is active.
events: A person submits one incorrect owner credential, producing a refused sign-in without reaching the lockout threshold.
Later, Kernel names an unregistered session.
outcomes: These events are outside the accepted gap because neither is one of the listed signs.
They are Registry-only refused attempts covered by the accepted gap and remain unseen.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions — changed since its latest review.
open_points.text: the infrastructure, to which they are ordinary HTTPS, sees only what it sees of its own
open_points.question: Which infrastructure component observes ordinary HTTPS, what request metadata or security events does it retain, for how long, and what—if anything—the owner can inspect in the first release?
options: The HTTPS proxy keeps owner-visible access logs containing limited metadata and status codes.
Infrastructure exposes only operational aggregates and no per-request record.
No infrastructure component retains or exposes any observation of these requests.
open_points.default_guess: Assume ordinary operational access logging may exist but provides no Registry-specific classification and is not relied on as a product security signal.

witness.initial: The first release is behind the owner's VPN and HTTPS termination.
events: A caller repeatedly sends service requests with an unknown token.
Registry refuses every request without recording it.
outcomes: The HTTPS infrastructure retains timestamps, source metadata, routes and response statuses that the owner can inspect.
The infrastructure retains nothing about the requests, so the attempts leave no observable evidence anywhere.
